While most of the post-copy steps are listed in the created `TODO.md` file
within the project, this documents some more details for these steps. Use this
guide alongside the `TODO.md` to complete those tasks. There are post-copy tasks
for two types of people: the person creating the project and the person who will
actually use it. Sometimes these are the same person, but in DP-Next they are
usually two different people. That's because we need to do some GitHub admin
tasks after creating the repository that only some people have access
permissions for. So this guide is split into those two people: **creator** and
**researcher**.

## Creator

### Setting up a GitHub repository

Before you can put the project on GitHub, you need to set up the project to be a
Git repository. Use these commands in the terminal to do that:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
git init -b main
git add .
git commit -m "start of project"
```

These commands will initialize the project as a Git repository (`init`) with
`main` as the main branch name and then will `add` and `commit` all the files
into the Git history. Now you're ready to upload to GitHub!

The easiest and quickest way to put the repository up onto the DP-Next GitHub
organization is to use the `gh` command line tool:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
gh repo create dp-next/REPO --source=. --public --push
```

This command creates a public repository on GitHub using the folder Git
repository (`.`) and then pushes the contents of the folder up to GitHub. The
next steps include some administrative tasks that make it easier to manage and
protect the repository. In [Seedcase](https://seedcase-project.org), we created
a custom command line tool to help manage GitHub repositories. While it's useful
for us, it isn't designed or build in a way that makes it easy for others to
use. So for this step, you can try to install our internal tool
[`spaid`](https://github.com/seedcase-project/spaid) and run the commands below.
Or you can ask Luke to do these next steps, as they are very quick to do.

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
spaid_gh_set_repo_settings dp-next/REPO
spaid_gh_ruleset_basic_protect_main dp-next/REPO
spaid_team_add_repo dp-next research-projects-team REPO
spaid_team_add_user dp-next research-projects-team USERNAME
```

Some configuration may be needed after copying this template to a new
repository, including configuration external to the repository. However, most of
these settings have already been set at the organizational level. For
informational purposes, the created workflow in
`.github/workflows/add-to-project.yml` of the newly created repository requires
the [add-to-board-token](https://github.com/apps/add-to-board-token) GitHub App
(a Seedcase app), along with the `ADD_TO_BOARD_TOKEN` secret and the
`ADD_TO_BOARD_APP_ID` variable of the GitHub App's ID. These can all be set in
the GitHub organization settings (and have already been set).
